spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The operative move is to compress all primes up to a cutoff into one additive quantity: theta sums their logarithms. Because logarithms turn products into sums, this is also a compact handle on the multiplicative mass of the cutoff prime set.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The unit defines the Chebyshev function theta(x) as the sum of log q over primes q less than or equal to x, with log denoting the natural logarithm.
directed.conceptual_reading: The definition replaces a varying collection of primes by a scalar aggregate. It preserves their total logarithmic, hence multiplicative, contribution while not retaining the contribution of each prime as a separately accessible object.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is prime cutoff to sum of logarithms to logarithm of the corresponding prime product. This lets a finite prime product be coupled to scalar growth expressions such as the Nicolas inequality and the auxiliary function f identified in the packet.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This span is only a definition: it supplies no estimate for theta, no convergence statement, and no RH implication by itself.
directed.uncertainty: The displayed sum is line-broken, but the adjacent prose explicitly recovers both the prime index and the range q less than or equal to x. Formula layout still warrants scan checking before exact reuse.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The two propositions turn an infinite Euler product into a finite cutoff object with a controlled remainder: zeta(2) fixes the full product, while exp(2/x) caps the factors omitted beyond x.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Proposition 1.1 states zeta(2) as the product over primes of q squared divided by q squared minus one, equal to pi squared over 6. Proposition 1.2 states that for x at least 3, the tail product over primes q greater than x is at most exp(2/x).
directed.conceptual_reading: This is a decomposition-and-control mechanism. A global Euler product is split at x, and the infinite part that was discarded is represented by a tail with an explicit upper envelope.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Writing zeta(2) as finite product times tail and applying the tail bound gives zeta(2) at most exp(2/x) times the finite product over q less than or equal to x. Thus a fixed analytic constant becomes comparable to a finite prime product with quantified slack.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The bounds concern only this Euler product. They do not control the Dedekind normalization or by themselves establish the later combined inequality. The propositions are cited rather than proved in the span.
directed.uncertainty: The product index and fractions, especially in Proposition 1.1, are visibly line-broken and should be verified against the scan before formal use, although the intended prime-product roles are recoverable from the text.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Nicolas's criterion replaces RH by a threshold test repeated at every prime cutoff. Its force lies not in a single estimate but in uniform validity of a finite prime-product inequality across all x.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Nicolas(x) is defined by the strict inequality product over primes q less than or equal to x of q divided by q minus one greater than e to the gamma times log theta(x). Proposition 1.3 states that this holds for all x at least 2 if and only if RH is true.
directed.conceptual_reading: The proposition is an exact reformulation: a global statement about zeta zeros is represented by a universal family of arithmetic inequalities. The universal quantifier is structural and cannot be replaced silently by success at selected cutoffs.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The finite Euler-type product measures multiplicative accumulation of the cutoff primes, while theta supplies the additive prime-log aggregate and log theta normalizes its scale. Their ratio against e to the gamma is the bridge object whose crossing of 1 encodes the criterion.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The criterion does not prove that the inequalities hold; it only states their equivalence to RH. It also depends on the preceding definition of theta, so the span is not semantically self-contained without that local setup.
directed.uncertainty: The factors, strict inequality, and exponentiated Euler constant are readable, but the displayed layout is extraction-sensitive and should be scan-checked for exact transcription.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The primorial M_x is the useful intermediate object: it encodes the whole prime cutoff as one squarefree integer, allowing the Dedekind psi product to be evaluated along a structured sequence and then normalized to a limiting constant.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The unit defines Psi(n) as n times the product over prime divisors q of n of 1 plus 1/q, defines M_x as the product of primes q less than or equal to x, and defines R(n) as Psi(n) divided by n log log n for n at least 3. Proposition 1.4 states unconditionally that R(M_x) tends to e to the gamma divided by zeta(2).
directed.conceptual_reading: Passing to M_x aligns the divisors in Psi with exactly the primes below x. Dividing by n removes the trivial size factor, and division by log log n exposes a stable asymptotic scale rather than raw growth.
directed.representation_or_bridge: For the squarefree input M_x, Psi(M_x)/M_x becomes the finite product over q less than or equal to x of 1 plus 1/q. R therefore bridges a cutoff prime product and an asymptotic constant involving the same zeta(2) that appears in the Euler-product comparison.
directed.boundary_or_failure: A limit identifies neither a rate of convergence nor the side from which R(M_x) approaches its limit. Those missing data are essential if the limit is multiplied by another factor whose surplus over its own limit vanishes.
directed.uncertainty: All three defining displays and the limit are fragmented by extraction. Their mathematical roles are supported by the surrounding prose, but exact normalized formulas should be verified against the scan.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The lemma is powered by incompatible quantifiers: false RH is said to force arbitrarily late positive spikes of log f, whereas the proposed envelope would impose a ceiling at every sufficiently large input. The contradiction needs no direct control of zeros once both behaviors are granted.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The unit defines f(x) as e to the gamma times log theta(x) times the product over primes q less than or equal to x of 1 minus 1/q. Lemma 2.1 claims RH follows if exp(2/sqrt(x)) is at least f(x) for all sufficiently large x. Its proof cites, under false RH, an Omega-plus lower behavior for log f, expands this into arbitrarily late y with log f(y) at least k times a power of y, and compares those values with 2/sqrt(y).
directed.conceptual_reading: This is a contrapositive obstruction argument. Instead of deriving RH directly, it proposes to exclude a characteristic failure behavior: recurrent lower excursions cannot coexist with a uniform eventual upper envelope.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The normalized product f packages the Nicolas-side quantities into a single positive function, and taking its logarithm puts the cited lower spikes and the logarithm of the proposed exponential ceiling on the same additive scale. The bridge is therefore infinitely often lower growth versus eventual pointwise domination.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The lemma is only a sufficient condition and does not establish the envelope it requires. Its validity also depends on the cited Omega-plus result and on the exact exponent threshold; neither is independently proved in this span.
directed.uncertainty: Extraction flattens the superscripts and the threshold on b, so the exact power condition cannot be transcribed safely from this artifact alone. The packet supports the comparison mechanism and the 2/sqrt(x) envelope, but exact exponents require scan verification.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The attempted proof factors the desired bound into two quantities with complementary limiting constants, but that compression exposes the decisive gap: convergence of the factors to constants does not control which side their product occupies when the available surplus shrinks to zero.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Using Lemma 2.1, the source rewrites the target as A_x times R(M_x) at least e to the gamma, where A_x is exp(2/sqrt(x)) times the finite product over primes q less than or equal to x of q squared divided by q squared minus one. It invokes the Euler-product and tail propositions to compare A_x with zeta(2), invokes R(M_x) asymptotic to e to the gamma divided by zeta(2), and then asserts the target eventually holds.
directed.conceptual_reading: The factorization is a natural bridge construction: one factor is controlled through the omitted Euler tail and the other through Dedekind-psi normalization, with limiting constants designed to multiply to e to the gamma. But matching limit constants is weaker than an eventual inequality at their product boundary.
directed.representation_or_bridge: A_x exposes whatever positive slack the exponential adjustment leaves over the full Euler product, while R(M_x) translates the primorial arithmetic into a normalized factor tending to the complementary constant. Closing the bridge would require a one-sided bound or a rate comparison showing that any deficit in R is dominated by the slack in A_x.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Even if A_x is above zeta(2), its surplus may vanish, while R(M_x) may approach its limit from below with a larger error. Therefore the displayed premises do not imply A_x R(M_x) is eventually at least e to the gamma. The informal much-greater-than symbol supplies no quantified margin that repairs this gap, so Theorem 3.1 is unsupported as written.
directed.uncertainty: The products, target inequality, and much-greater-than display are extraction-sensitive and should be checked against the scan. The logical limitation remains under the roles and asymptotic relation recorded in the bounded packet.
